title: No recommendations in police shooting: Knife-wielding schizophrenic attacked two officers: [FINAL C Edition]
article: A jury at a coroner's inquest into the shooting death of a mentally ill man by a Vancouver police officer has offered no recommendations to prevent a similar result.

The members of the two-man, three-woman jury heard the dramatic testimony of how two officers with less than four years experience between them went from answering a routine call to killing the man in less than 30 seconds.
Vancouver police Const. John Filippelli testified he shot Dean Nicholas Andrusyk, 49, in 2004, after Andrusyk stabbed his partner, Const. Craig Look, three times.
Andrusyk died two hours later in hospital.
The officers approached Andrusyk under the mistaken belief he had called them about a domestic dispute.
Andrusyk attacked Look with a knife, cutting him deeply near his wrist.
Filippelli, who had three years on the force, told the inquest he thought Andrusyk was going to kill them both.
The jury listed "gunshot to the abdomen" as cause of death and paranoid schizophrenia as a "contributory factor." They classified the death as "homicide."
